quizName: DMV Practice Test #10 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: When riding behind a car, where should you position yourself?

options.text: Position yourself so the driver can see you in their rearview mirror.
Ride on the far left side of the lane.
Ride on the far right side of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Position yourself so the driver can see you in their rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Position yourself in the center of the lane so the driver can see you in their rearview mirror. This is where drivers are most likely to notice you.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle, what is the correct rule?

options.text: Complete the pass without exceeding the speed limit.
You can complete the pass in a no passing zone if you started before the zone began.
You can exceed the speed limit when passing.
Pass on the shoulder of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Complete the pass without exceeding the speed limit.
questions.explanation: Always complete passes within the speed limit and only in areas where passing is allowed.

questions.question: A wobble or shaking of the front wheel and handlebars may be caused by:

options.text: Brakes that are not working properly.

questions.explanation: Wobbles are usually caused by improper loading, unsuitable accessories, or incorrect tire pressure.

questions.question: Before changing lanes, what should you do?

options.text: Turn your head to check for vehicles in your blind spot.
Rely only on your mirrors to see your surroundings.
Point in the direction you are changing lanes.
Speed up to get ahead of other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head to check for vehicles in your blind spot.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots. Always turn your head to check for traffic in your blind spot before changing lanes. Do not rely on mirrors alone.

questions.question: What should passengers do when riding on a motorcycle?

options.text: Sit as far back on the bike as possible.

questions.explanation: Passengers should sit directly behind the operator and lean as the operator leans. Sit as far forward as possible without crowding the operator, and hold onto the operator's waist, hips, or belt.

questions.question: At what point does alcohol impair your riding ability?

options.text: Once you reach the legal limit.

questions.explanation: Never ride after drinking any amount of alcohol. Impairment begins well below the legal limit.

questions.question: When approaching a blind intersection, where should you ride?

options.text: Position yourself so other drivers see you as soon as possible.
Always ride in the left lane to stay farthest from oncoming traffic.
Slowly creep up to the intersection.
Weave slightly in your lane so your headlight is more visible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Position yourself so other drivers see you as soon as possible.
questions.explanation: When approaching a blind intersection, move to the part of the lane where oncoming drivers will see you earliest. For example, when approaching a blind corner to your right, stay in the left portion of your lane so you are seen sooner.

questions.question: When carrying a passenger in a sidecar, how should you brake?

options.text: Apply brakes more firmly to stop quickly.
Apply brakes more softly to avoid overworking them.

questions.explanation: The extra weight of a passenger in a sidecar affects handling. Your motorcycle needs more distance to stop completely.

questions.question: When riding in a group, what is the best formation to keep close while staying safe?
questions.explanation: A staggered formation keeps the group close while maintaining safe spacing for all riders. Use single-file when riding in curves, turning, or entering or leaving a highway. Never ride side-by-side.

questions.question: When riding over rough surfaces, how should you hold the handgrips?

options.text: Hold them loosely to allow for movement.
Hold them firmly to maintain control.
Use lots of throttle to get over the rough surface.
Ride without a helmet so it does not block your face.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold them firmly to maintain control.
questions.explanation: Hold the handgrips firmly when riding over rough surfaces. This keeps your motorcycle under control.

questions.question: What is the best way to stop quickly?

options.text: Reduce throttle and use the front brake.
Use both brakes at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: To stop quickly, squeeze both brakes at the same time. Apply them firmly and stay calm if the brakes lock up.

questions.question: What should you do about riding gloves?

options.text: Do not wear them because they make your hands too hot.
Wear them to get a better grip on the handlebars.
Do not wear them because they make it harder to use the controls.
Wear them only on cool days.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wear them to get a better grip on the handlebars.
questions.explanation: Wear leather gloves or gloves made of other tough material when riding. They improve your grip on the handlebars and protect your hands if you crash.

questions.question: What is an example of a rectangular sign?
questions.explanation: Signs that tell drivers about road rules, like speed limits, are usually rectangular. They are white with black letters or symbols. You must follow the rules on these signs.

questions.question: Where is the front brake lever usually found?
questions.explanation: The front brake lever is usually on the right handlebar. Learn where all your motorcycle's controls are before you start riding.

questions.question: When you are about to pass another vehicle on the left, what should you do?

options.text: Stay in the right part of your lane.
Stay in the left part of your lane.
Get as close as possible to the vehicle in front.
Do not signal, as it may distract the driver you are passing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in the left part of your lane.
questions.explanation: When passing on the left, stay in the left part of your lane. Signal first and check for traffic. Pass when it is safe, then signal again and return to your lane.

questions.question: Why should you check your motorcycle before riding?

options.text: It is useless unless a mechanic does it.
You should not check it before riding.
You should only check it after riding.
It helps you find any mechanical problems or broken equipment.

questions.correctAnswerText: It helps you find any mechanical problems or broken equipment.
questions.explanation: Check your motorcycle thoroughly before every ride. This helps you find any problems that could be dangerous.

questions.question: What blood alcohol concentration (BAC) makes a person legally intoxicated?
questions.explanation: In Kentucky, a BAC of 0.08 percent or higher means a person is legally intoxicated. It is illegal and dangerous to drive while intoxicated.

questions.question: Before riding, check all of the following except:

options.text: How much tread is on your tires.
The condition of your tire sidewalls.

questions.explanation: Before every ride, check your tire air pressure, tire tread wear, and the overall condition of your tire sidewalls and treads.

questions.question: What are the penalties for drinking and riding?

options.text: Left up to a judge to decide.

questions.explanation: Oregon law has very strict required penalties for drinking and riding. It is illegal and dangerous to ride while intoxicated.

questions.question: When should you increase your following distance?

options.text: If there are only a few vehicles on the road.
If drivers are following the speed limit.

questions.explanation: Leave more space between you and the vehicle ahead if your motorcycle needs more distance to stop. Increase your following distance if the pavement is slippery, if you cannot see ahead clearly, or if traffic is heavy.

questions.question: When changing lanes, what should you do?

options.text: Signal, check your mirrors, and turn your head.
Turn your head and change lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, check your mirrors, and turn your head.
questions.explanation: Always signal before changing lanes. Check your mirrors and turn your head to look for traffic around your motorcycle before you move.

questions.question: When riding at night, what should you do?

options.text: Get closer to the vehicle ahead.
Stay farther from the vehicle ahead.
Do not use your high beam headlight.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay farther from the vehicle ahead.
questions.explanation: It is harder to see distances in the dark. Slow down and stay farther from the vehicle ahead when riding at night. Use your high beam when you are not meeting or following another vehicle.

questions.question: Which body part operates the gearshift lever?
questions.explanation: The gearshift lever is in front of the left footrest. You operate it with your left foot.

questions.question: When should you increase your following distance?

options.text: When you can see through the vehicle ahead.

questions.explanation: Increase your distance from the vehicle ahead if your motorcycle needs more space to stop. Also increase your distance in heavy traffic or when you cannot see past the vehicle in front of you.

questions.question: How many alcoholic drinks can affect a rider's ability to ride?
questions.explanation: Just one alcoholic drink can affect your ability to ride. Riding under the influence of alcohol is illegal and dangerous.
